exposure: Mode of delivery (elective cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Presence of Bifidobacterium in meconium and transitional stool
Cord blood cytokine levels (IL-1β, IL-10, IL-6, GM-CSF, IL-5, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2, IL-4 and IL-8)
cohort: 89 mother-newborn pairs (23 vaginal delivery and 66 elective cesarean delivery) in Southern Brazil
finding: Compared to vaginally-delivered neonates, Cesarean-delivered neonates had lower leukocyte counts, lower hemoglobin levels, lower cord blood GM-CSF levels, and were less likely to have Bifidobacterium detected in their transitional stool.
